title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that same candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real (production-like) confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition that was actually run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived as described in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), producing CLI sequences from operator intents. Stochastic generation, however, risks syntactic errors, wrong command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties that can produce unsafe or nonfunctional changes. Prior surveys and empirical work document feasible draft-generation but repeatedly recommend deterministic verification and bounded repair or human oversight to reduce mechanically verifiable defects [1],[2].

A common mitigation architecture interposes a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which rejects or attempts constrained fixes for validator-detected defects [3],[4]. GVR pipelines are known to reduce mechanically checkable errors (syntax, ordering, local-policy), but it remains an open empirical question how large the marginal verifier-and-repair effect is when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained tasks.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation plus a single permitted repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics: the same LLM-generated candidate is evaluated both without (baseline) and with (guarded) the validator+repair pipeline. By holding the generated candidate fixed across conditions we measure only the validator-and-repair marginal outcome on identical model outputs. Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal effect for a constrained NetOps task bank (N_pairs = 250) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps and LLM surveys establish three points relevant to this study: (a) LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups but often require verification or human oversight [1],[2]; (b) deterministic verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., Batfish and header-space techniques) provide mechanized checks for forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[5]; and (c) generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, though semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [4],[6].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize filtering and validation layers but note adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [7]. Our study differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across conditions), by providing complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation for stage-level mapping of generation and repair calls, and by archiving comprehensive validator traces and reconciliations so the numeric outcomes are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the study as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). The confirmatory design was a paired binary comparison with N_pairs = 250 and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration fixed shared_initial_candidate semantics, a single permitted automated repair per episode, exclusion rules, and the primary analysis (exact McNemar two‑sided plus paired-bootstrap CIs).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (explicit statement and reconciliation). Consistent with the preregistration, exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and the identical generated candidate was reused for both baseline and guarded episodes; no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call accounting reconciles model_calls_used = 251 as 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call. The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) records provider_call_audit with hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} (SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3). The adapter labels observed in the audit (for example condition_counts = {"shared": 250, "guarded": 1}) reflect adapter-internal bookkeeping: the label "shared" records the single shared initial-generation stage events (one per intent), while the single "guarded" labeled model call corresponds to the single repair-stage call recorded under stage_counts = {"repair": 1}. We state this mapping explicitly to avoid misinterpretation that multiple independent guarded-generation calls were made.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe-access transfer patterns) and protected interfaces that must not be modified. The full task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

Model, validator, and repair policy. All initial generations used declared_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version: gpt-5-mini). The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering, evaluating workflow constraints, constructing a final_state snapshot, and returning a boolean valid flag plus diagnostic fields (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes). When valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one automated deterministic repair attempt using template-driven transformations restricted to syntactic and ordering fixes (reorder commands to required_sequence, split/join lines, correct obvious token ordering). Repaired outputs were re-validated once; no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed by preregistration.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Exclusion rules removed items failing vendor-parser deterministically such that verification was impossible, items with credential-like tokens, or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens or private-address artifacts; flagged items were to be excluded from primary analysis and handled in sensitivity analyses. In the executed confirmatory partition no episodes were excluded or flagged and complete_pair_count = 250.

Primary analysis. The preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executed the primary test (exact two-sided McNemar) and computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500 and completed_episode_count = 500 (complete_pair_count = 250). Provider-call accounting reconciles model_calls_used = 251: 250 shared_initial_generation calls and 1 repair call (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3). Contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes and no preregistered exclusions were applied.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The single discordant pair (baseline fail, guarded pass) corresponds to the one exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returns p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These analysis artifacts and bootstrap parameters are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Representative validator diagnostics and repair trace. Validator traces for passed episodes include parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to the task's required_sequence length; for example, task-000003 (hard) shows parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, valid = true in both baseline and guarded episodes (execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json). Only one automated repair occurred; its repair trace and the guarded scoring artifact for that pair are archived in the raw_results manifest. No other repairs were needed for the confirmatory partition.

Missingness. No episodes were excluded from the primary analysis: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 250 and all other missingness counts = 0. Contamination summary is empty for the confirmatory partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus one automated repair was small: gpt-5-mini initial candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the only failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum plausible verifier-improvement under these conditions.

Artifact-grounded reasons for small observed gain. The small guarded gain is explained artifact-groundedly by: (1) constrained tasks produced by a deterministic generator that reduced verbal ambiguity and limited allowed_touched_fields and required_sequence (execution/task_manifest.jsonl); (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these task constraints (execution/raw_results.jsonl); and (3) the deterministic validator checked mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required ordering, and expected_final_state snapshots) but did not assess live protocol dynamics or emergent cross-device behaviors.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 and targeted detecting a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ~80% power; realized baseline = 0.996 substantially exceeded this assumption, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements. Therefore, the paired-bootstrap CI bounding the maximum verifier-detected benefit is the most informative result for practitioners under comparable constraints.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness and does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised. These limitations constrain generalization beyond the executed partition.

Operational implications (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small; this finding does not imply validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts. Validators that check properties not exercised here (vendor-specific forwarding invariants, dynamic protocol invariants) or multi-iteration repair/human escalation could show larger benefits. Production heterogeneity and adaptive attackers could materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the marginal verifier-detected benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived as described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and key artifacts: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is the only master-prompt SHA disclosed here. Execution reconciled model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation + 1 repair) as recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256: 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3).

Archived manifest: the full execution and analysis bundle (raw responses, execution manifest, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript) is archived in the run's evidence bundle; the archive includes execution/execution_manifest.json and the preregistration and reconciliation artifacts cited above. The archive is the authoritative machine-verifiable record for reproducing the numeric claims in this paper.

Preregistered vs executed estimand: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a planned sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in Results is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
